nodes.label: globalSetup fixture seeding
nodes.rationale: Seeds a verified ADMIN account and an `e2e` project whose cases (seq 1-4) map to TC-E2E-<n> names, so specs start from a deterministic database state.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation on API key membership
nodes.norm_label: tenant isolation on api key membership
nodes.rationale: The API key's user must be a member of the target project, so a key cannot write runs into a project outside its tenant.

nodes.label: TestForge REST API v1 (frozen, supported)
nodes.rationale: v1 is frozen but explicitly not deprecated, so existing integrations keep working unchanged rather than being forced onto v2.

nodes.label: TestForge REST API v2
nodes.rationale: v2 adds resources v1 never exposed (milestones, members, webhooks), uniform pagination and project-scoped keys.

nodes.label: paginate (items/meta cursor walking)
nodes.rationale: Every collection returns a uniform { items, meta } envelope, so one async-iterator helper can walk any list operation.

nodes.label: Per-key rate limit tracking and 429 retry
nodes.norm_label: per-key rate limit tracking and 429 retry
nodes.rationale: Each API key has its own per-minute budget; the client reads the limit headers from the latest response and retries 429s up to maxRetries (default 2) honouring Retry-After.

nodes.label: TestForgeApiError
nodes.rationale: Carries the API's stable machine code (e.g. validation_error) so callers branch on codes instead of parsing prose messages.

nodes.label: gate command (CI quality gate verdict)
nodes.rationale: Exits 0 only when the gate passes - any failure OR an error reaching the server exits 1, so a broken gate blocks the pipeline rather than waving builds through.

nodes.label: Quality Gate policy (Fields → Quality Gate)
nodes.rationale: Policy lives server-side (min pass rate, max new failures vs previous run, block-on-untested, required tags) so CI only enforces a verdict it does not define.

nodes.label: TC-<SLUG>-<n> case-matching convention
nodes.rationale: Tests are matched to cases by a TC-<SLUG>-<n> annotation in the test name, falling back to an exact title match when absent.

nodes.label: TESTFORGE_URL / TESTFORGE_TOKEN env contract
nodes.rationale: Every command reads connection settings from the environment (or --url/--token); upload and push need a WRITE-scoped key while gate, pull and status only need READ.

nodes.label: upload command (multi-format results)
nodes.rationale: Accepts JUnit, TRX, NUnit3, xUnit.net v2, Cucumber JSON and Mocha JSON, auto-detecting the format unless forced with --format, so any CI toolchain can report without conversion.

nodes.label: Cypress state → TestForge status mapping
nodes.rationale: passed → PASSED, pending/skipped → SKIPPED, failed → FAILED; the display error truncated to 5000 chars becomes the result comment.

nodes.label: Playwright status → TestForge status mapping
nodes.rationale: passed → PASSED, skipped → SKIPPED, failed/timedOut/interrupted → FAILED; the failure message truncated to 5000 chars becomes the result comment, and tests without a TC- id are skipped but counted in the summary line.

nodes.label: TC id anywhere in the pytest node id
nodes.norm_label: tc id anywhere in the pytest node id
nodes.rationale: The id may live in the function name or in a parametrization id, so cases can be bound either per-test or per-parameter.

nodes.label: pytest outcome → TestForge status mapping
nodes.rationale: passed → PASSED, skipped → SKIPPED, failed → FAILED; the failure traceback truncated to 5000 chars becomes the result comment.

nodes.label: E2E Playwright suite (dogfooding TestForge)
nodes.rationale: The suite runs against a local dev server and uploads its own results back into TestForge so the product exercises its own /api/v1/junit ingestion path.

nodes.label: TestForgeClient
nodes.rationale: Zero runtime dependencies on Node 18+ built-in fetch, with one fully typed method per API operation.

nodes.label: testforge-cli
nodes.rationale: Command-line uploader for CI and for keeping test cases in git; Node 18+ using built-in fetch.

nodes.label: testforge-playwright-reporter
nodes.rationale: Streams live: opens a run when the suite starts, posts each test result as it finishes, and completes the run at the end.

nodes.label: pytest-testforge plugin
nodes.rationale: Auto-registers with pytest and streams results (run opened at session start, per-test posts, completion at the end); zero dependencies, Python 3.8+, standard library only.

nodes.label: Fixed E2E API key upserted by hash
nodes.norm_label: fixed e2e api key upserted by hash
nodes.rationale: The token is upserted by its hash so concurrent runs converge on one row instead of revoking each other; it is written to e2e-results/.api-key for the upload script while specs read E2E.apiKey directly.

nodes.label: Env-driven upload target (TF_API_URL / TF_PROJECT / TF_API_KEY)
nodes.rationale: All plumbing is env-driven so reporting a locally-run suite to production needs no code change - only pointing TF_API_URL/TF_PROJECT/TF_API_KEY at prod.

nodes.label: Token-free deterministic E2E (no model in the loop)
nodes.norm_label: token-free deterministic e2e (no model in the loop)
nodes.rationale: Because no Claude model participates, the tests cost no tokens and are safe to run repeatedly or wire into CI.

nodes.label: OpenAPI-driven client generation
nodes.rationale: generated/ is checked in so consumers never run the generator; it is re-run and committed whenever src/lib/openapi-v2.ts changes in the main app, emitting types.d.ts, client.js and client.d.ts while everything in src/ stays hand-written.

nodes.label: Project-scoped API keys
nodes.rationale: A key bound to one project returns 403 forbidden for every other project even one its owning user belongs to - so CI can hold a token that cannot reach beyond the repo it builds.

nodes.label: Test cases as code (YAML in git)
nodes.norm_label: test cases as code (yaml in git)
nodes.rationale: A tests/ folder of canonical YAML is synced with the server so cases are reviewed in pull requests like code; full schema and merge semantics live in docs/CASES-AS-CODE.md.

nodes.label: .testforge.lock 3-way merge base
nodes.rationale: A committed lock file holds the base state for 3-way merging; conflicting edits exit 1 with a report rather than silently overwriting either side, with --force-local/--force-server as explicit opt-outs.

nodes.label: Cypress plugin fail-safe no-op
nodes.rationale: If URL, token or project is missing the plugin logs a warning and does nothing - reporting must never fail the user's test run.

nodes.label: setupNodeEvents plugin over Mocha reporter
nodes.rationale: Implemented as a setupNodeEvents plugin rather than a Mocha reporter because Cypress re-instantiates Mocha reporters per spec, which makes a single streamed run and async network posts unreliable; the plugin runs once per cypress run in the Node process, opening the run at before:run, posting at after:spec and completing at after:run.

nodes.label: Playwright reporter fail-safe no-op
nodes.rationale: If URL, token or project is missing the reporter logs a warning and does nothing - it never fails the test run.

nodes.label: pytest plugin fail-safe no-op
nodes.rationale: If URL, token and project are not all set the plugin does nothing - it never fails the test run.
